free_tier.stated: The Starter plan is free forever with no time limit: 2 development environments on Encore Cloud, 1M tracing events a month, 7-day log and trace retention, 1 concurrent build. Applications hosted on Encore Cloud carry fair-use limits per application on every plan: 100,000 requests a day, 100,000 Pub/Sub messages a day, 1 GB of database storage, 1 GB of object storage, and cron jobs no more often than once an hour.

interface_detail: the encore CLI, documented in the CLI reference at encore.dev/docs/ts/cli/cli-reference
tooling: the Encore CLI (encore auth login; git push encore to deploy; encore gen client generates Go, TypeScript and JavaScript API clients)
chaining: 100k requests a day of a free hosted Go or TypeScript API with 1 GB of managed Postgres behind it is a whole small service for nothing; the hourly-cron ceiling means a tighter loop has to move, and on Pro the compute moves to a user's own AWS account.

limits.value: 100,000 requests a day is the ceiling, about 1.16 requests a second averaged, and cron at most hourly means a polling loop cannot be tightened.

evidence.proved: the CLI logs in and deploys through a git remote
evidence.quote: Requires `encore auth login`. Clones into a directory named after the app ID by default, with a git remote named `encore`, so you can deploy changes with `git push encore`.

notes: The unit is requests, not compute: Encore publishes no vCPU or memory allowance for the free hosted environment, so the shape is null rather than guessed. Not established, since the page names deployment to your own cloud as a Pro feature without saying Starter is blocked from Encore Cloud hosting. That is the open question and it moves the verdict between qualifies and trial-only.
